title: Strategy Form
description: A runnable backtest request. The LLM fills this from a plain-English prompt; the engine only accepts forms that validate. Percent values are positive numbers in percent (40 = a 40% drawdown). Custom annotations: x-ask = when the LLM should ask the user (always | if_ambiguous | never); x-default = the literal value used when the user says nothing, always one the job can honour; x-default-note = a description of a default that depends on the rest of the form, for a reader rather than a program.

prompt.description: The user's original request, verbatim. Kept so the insight step can answer the question that was actually asked.

template.description: Which strategy template the strategy block follows. More templates (indicator_crossover, periodic_rebalance, dca) are added later as new enum values plus a matching oneOf branch in strategy.

price_adjustment.description: total_return reinvests dividends; split_only ignores them.

warmup_days.description: History loaded before start so lookback windows (e.g. a 252-day high) are populated on day one. Trades never occur during warmup.

cash.description: What uninvested cash earns while the strategy waits for a signal. Matters a lot for entry-timing strategies that sit in cash for years.

fixed_rate_pct.description: Annual rate, required when yield = fixed.

fill.description: Signals are computed on a bar's close; fills happen on a later bar. Same-bar fills are deliberately not offered because they are look-ahead.

objective.description: What 'optimal' means. Only used to rank results when any strategy parameter is a sweep; every metric is still reported.

metric.description: Higher is better, except ulcer_index, where lower is. max_drawdown is negative, so higher means shallower (JOB.md section 5).

min_trades.description: Parameter sets with fewer completed entries than this are excluded from ranking (still shown, flagged).

benchmarks.description: Symbols held buy-and-hold over the same range for comparison. Synthetic extensions in universe apply to benchmarks with the same symbol.

oos_split.description: Optimize on [start, date), report the chosen parameters on [date, end]. null disables.
oos_split.x-default-note: the date 60% of the way through the range

regime_breakdown.description: Report performance inside each catalog regime (list_regimes) that overlaps the range.

parameter_surface.description: Return the objective for every swept parameter value so the insight step can tell a plateau from a spike.

provenance.description: Where each value came from, keyed by JSON Pointer into this form (e.g. "/strategy/entry/threshold_pct"). The engine ignores this; the UI uses it to flag values and the LLM uses it to decide what to ask. A path whose source is 'missing' must be resolved before the form is submitted.

param.description: A numeric strategy parameter: a fixed value, an inclusive range sweep, or an explicit list. Any sweep makes the run an optimization ranked by objective.metric.

symbol.description: The ticker as the user knows it. Display only.

security_id.description: From the catalog's resolve(symbol, date_range.start). What the engine actually loads.

synthetic_extension.description: Extend history before the asset's inception by simulating it from an underlying: daily_return = leverage * underlying_return - (fee + (leverage - 1) * (cash_rate + borrow_spread)) / 252. Spliced at the first real bar. The insight step must say which part of the range is synthetic.

recipe_id.description: The catalog recipe these parameters were copied from. The engine checks they still match it.

drawdown_reference.description: The high that drawdown is measured from.

type.description: Highest close since the start of loaded data (including warmup and synthetic history).
Highest close over the trailing window, e.g. 252 for a 52-week high.
Highest close since the strategy last sold; falls back to all_time_high before the first trade.

exit_rule.description: One exit condition. A position is sold when any of its rules fires.

type.description: Sell when price regains the reference high that was in force at entry.

drawdown_entry.description: Sit in cash; buy when the asset falls a given percent below a reference high; sell per the exit rules.

style.description: Invest position_pct of equity once the drawdown reaches threshold_pct.
Scale in: each tranche buys its fraction of starting equity when its drawdown level is first reached. Fractions must sum to at most 100.

rules.description: Empty means buy and hold forever after entry.

reentry.description: After an exit, may the strategy buy again on the next qualifying drawdown? Irrelevant when exit.rules is empty.

source.description: stated: the user said it. inferred: the LLM read it from context. default: the system assumption. missing: required and unknown.

quote.description: The prompt text a stated or inferred value came from.

note.description: Why a value was inferred, or a warning to surface (e.g. inception date shorter than the requested range).

options.description: For missing fields: the choices to offer the user as buttons.
